newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador aims to sell telephone co by April.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador aims to sell telephone co by April.

text.p: The government of El Salvador said on Tuesday that it plans to sell 61 per cent of the shares of the state telephone company before April.
The sale of the telephone company, National Telecommunications Administration (ANTEL), is part of a widespread sell-off of public companies by the government.
The company has been valued at about $326 million.
The president of ANTEL, Juan Jose Daboub, told reporters that the price would be determined by a public auction before the end of March.
At that time 51 percent of the shares will be sold to a majority group of buyers, called "strategic partners".
"We have offered the company to the biggest telecommunications companies in the world," Daboub said.
He said that 10 percent will be sold to ANTEL workers.
The other 39 percent of the shares will placed with a trust that will sell the shares locally or on the international market within four years, company officials said.

Officials said that legislation that will start the process of converting ANTEL into two private companies will be ready by December. The ownership structure will be the same for each of the two companies.
They said that the privatization could help fill a deficit of 300,000 telephone lines in the country.
